summary: R J Sanderson & Associates is a Dandenong-headquartered accounting, tax, wealth and advisory group that has grown by acquisition, most recently merging Paynter & Associates in Myrtleford in 2025 and describing itself as nearly 130 professionals across 15 offices. Roy Sanderson is the founding Managing Director, still current, and a regular radio tax commentator. The firm publishes its software stack (Xero XPM, FYI, BGL, Ignition and others) for merger partners, sells Xero and Hubdoc bookkeeping packages, and advertised a senior bookkeeper role in October 2026. That makes it a stronger fit than its tax-heavy profile suggested.

claims.quote: join our expanding bookkeeping team working in the Mornington Peninsual and accross all our locations

claims.quote: CPA, Guest Speaker on Tax & Business, Radio & TV Presenter, MC, Mentor, Awarded Best Accounting & Advisory Firm 2019 & 2020

claims.text: In 2023 Roy was announced as a fortnightly guest on 3AW's 'Tax Talk' and on RPPFM Peninsula Radio, taking listener tax questions.
claims.quote: Roy Sanderson will be joining Darren James on 3AW every second Saturday at 9.45 am to discuss taxes and take questions from listeners.

claims.text: RJS describes a Mornington senior partner and manager as a CPA who assists with how to create efficiencies through the use of technology and tightening internal processes.
claims.quote: She assists with strategies on how to can create efficiencies through the use of technology, tightening internal processes

hooks.text: Serial acquirer that publishes its own software stack for merger partners; each acquired office adds a new set of bank feeds and coding habits that must be reconciled and standardised.
Live bookkeeper hiring in October 2026 with bank reconciliation named in the duties: the reconciliation load is growing faster than headcount.
Xero + Hubdoc bookkeeping packages sold by transaction volume: efficiency per client directly protects margin.

risks.text: The firm is large (nearly 130 people) and tax- and wealth-heavy; Roy is a high-profile MD, so a central ops or technology lead may own the tooling decision and the email could be forwarded.

Existing stack already includes Hubdoc and Xero XPM, and the firm is part of a wider group (the Modoras Group is named in RJS's financial services guide), so a group-level standard may constrain new tools.
Merger activity may mean systems are being consolidated now, which could help or delay a pilot.

gaps: No podcast or YouTube interview by Roy within the last 12 months found; the 3AW and RPPFM segments date from 2023.
No Karbon, Dext or AI reconciliation tool mention found.
No LinkedIn posts by Roy retrieved.
Could not confirm the Modoras Group relationship beyond the financial services guide, so it was left out of claims.
